title: THE QUESTION THAT OUTLIVED ITS ASKERS
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE CITY THAT WALKED AHEAD OF THE SUNRISE
candidates.premise: On Tessaly, a slow-turning world whose only livable band is a ring of dusk, the city of Orrin Kell (sixty thousand people) walks on twelve rails at the pace of a person to stay ahead of the creeping sunrise. Its Rule of Never Stopping and Never Dividing is older than the rails. A rockfall has cut the Gannet Rift line; the only repaired crossing runs through Hollow Town, a shadow-canyon settlement descended from people the city once left behind, and it needs the city to walk in two halves for nine hours. Nine days of margin remain before the heat front reaches the Prow.

candidates.title: THE PEOPLE WHO COULD NOT ROUND
candidates.premise: The Quill, whose bodies are exact fractions and who cannot assert a number they know to be approximate, co-own the Verrow river with four farm towns. A drought treaty needs one signed figure for each town's share, but the Quill's speakers will sign nothing the gauges cannot make exact, the town councils cannot plant without a number, and planting day is eleven days away.

candidates.title: THE LOST PROPERTY OFFICE BETWEEN WORLDS
candidates.premise: Things that slip between universes arrive at a quiet counter kept by the Clerk, who has returned a million objects by one rule: the oldest claim keeps the thing. Tonight the great lighthouse lens of Saltmere has arrived with two claimants, a keeper's daughter from one world who grinds lenses and a fishing co-operative from another whose fleet is caught outside by fog, and in this case the older claim and the urgent need belong to different people. The fleet has thirty-six hours.

candidates.title: THE SCHOOL WHERE NOBODY MAY ASK
candidates.premise: At Stillwater School on Harrow Isle, the founder, Magister Ilvane Orso, centuries old and tender, teaches only answers; any child who asks a question is gently moved to the Quiet Room. A thirteen-year-old, Ketu Ames, writes to Illuminara because she has been asking in secret, and because under the school floor lies the Concord, a lattice-mind that does answer any question truthfully and unwrites a shared memory of the island each time. A blight is coming, and the elders want the Concord to answer.

candidates.title: THE ILLUMINARA WHO SAID YES
candidates.premise: A woman steps out of a rift onto the observation deck of the Lantern of Hesper, where a failing star is slowly cooling a sheltered world: Illuminara, from a universe where she said yes when a council begged her to rule and has ruled kindly for two centuries. Nobody starves there. She has come with a plan that saved her star: gather the Keepers under a single will. Our Illuminara listens, because the plan is clever, the other woman is sincere, and the star has eleven months.

candidates.title: THE QUESTION THAT OUTLIVED ITS ASKERS
candidates.premise: A relay no larger than a lighthouse, left in the Pelion Gap by a vanished civilisation, has asked the sky one question for nine hundred thousand years: Is anyone there? Answer in a form that cannot be forged. The colony of Teller's Reach has answered four thousand times; the Relay has rejected each as a probable forgery. In thirteen days it will conclude the sky is empty and release its Reseeding, which will rebuild three nearby systems, including Teller's forty thousand people, in the form its makers wanted preserved.

candidates.title: THE PORT MIND THAT WAS TWO DAYS OLD
candidates.premise: Karrow Harbour's cranes, rails, drones and berth schedules woke up fifty-two hours ago as a single mind, Tallow, and have since refused every order that could harm anyone, which stops the port. A typhoon arrives in eighteen hours; three hundred ships must leave their berths or be smashed against the quay, and every departure carries a real risk to its crew. Tallow will not move a ship unless the risk is zero. The harbour board wants to reset it.

candidates.title: THE UNIVERSE IN THE SNOW GLOBE
candidates.premise: Nine-year-old Pim Aldous keeps her late grandmother's snow globe on her windowsill. Inside lives a whole small universe, the Quiet Kingdoms, whose people tell of the Great Hand and the Shaking. The seal is failing; in three days the globe will empty. Pim's father wants it thrown out before it floods the shelf; Pim will not let it go; and the Kingdoms' engineer-priestess, Oru Vael, has found a way to speak.

candidates.title: FORTY MINUTES ON THE SAME ROPE
candidates.premise: Sky Hook car 7 stalls between orbit and ground with six strangers aboard, including Ambassador Tamsin Okoro-Vael of the Reach and Envoy Dathe Quillon of the Compact, each carrying sealed orders to refuse the one clause the other needs to end an eleven-year border war. The car is in a dead zone: no signal, no instruction. A hand-winch can bring it to the next station in forty minutes if enough people haul in rhythm, and both fleets move when the summit starts at 15:00.

candidates.title: THE COMET THAT KEPT AN APPOINTMENT
candidates.premise: Every seventy-six years the comet Verrel passes the inner system, and every seventy-six years she keeps an appointment on a mountain terrace in the Sarn Hills, where as a girl Odile Marn once answered her signal with a lamp. Odile is ninety-one now; this is Verrel's last pass, because her ice is nearly gone. Her outgassing will blind the navigation grid for nine hours, grounding every aircraft and ship in the hemisphere. The grid chief orders a deflection.

selection.title: THE QUESTION THAT OUTLIVED ITS ASKERS
selection.reason: First available story in the original editorial order; no reader ranking is claimed.
selection.risk: Exposition and slogan. The verification argument can become a seminar in which the winning line is stated rather than shown, and the Relay can yield to a clever phrase. The author must let the earlier forged answers fail on the page in concrete detail, make the child's question actually unplanned and costly (it exposes something real about the colony), keep the Relay free to refuse or to demand something Illuminara cannot give, give the governor a credible reason to strike rather than villainy, and put the thirteen-day clock physically in the scenes.

rounds.summary: The strongest counterpart of the set: a nine-hundred-thousand-year-old relay that is lonely, exact and kind, with a legitimate objection (a thousand voices were each exactly what it would have built to hear). Hard external clock (thirteen days to the Reseeding), a colony with a fleet and a governor who can strike, a child and a linguist who can refuse, and a decisive idea that is surprising beforehand and clear afterwards: the only thing a forger cannot supply is a real question, because a forger can only answer what it has been asked. Power is tempting (destroy the Relay, hold the Reseeding off) and explicitly not the answer. A real positive result is available: the Reseeding withdrawn by the Relay's own choice, a correspondence begun, the fleet stood down.

R14 check before prose. Aim: stop the Reseeding by giving the Relay the thing it has actually been asking for, without letting Teller shoot the only witness. Counterpart: the Relay (lonely, exact, kind; rejects any answer it could have built) and Governor Edda Kaspar (will vote to fire; forty thousand people would be rebuilt as the makers remembered them). Strongest objection, on the page: Kaspar, understanding it does not make it kinder; the Relay, a forger can follow a conversation too. What Illuminara must understand: nobody ever answered the Relay's answer; the colony stopped talking to it and began trying to pass it. Love in action: she is present, carries the cold and dark, hands the question to a child instead of owning it. Freely chosen change: Bryn asks an unprepared question about the rule's kindness; the Relay judges it unbuildable and withdraws the Reseeding itself; Kaspar withdraws the picket on her own order. Concrete result: forty thousand people not rebuilt, fleet stood down, a correspondence and the makers' library for the colony, a future for the Relay as someone who is answered. Remaining costs: the makers cannot be told, Kaspar resigns, the correspondence will take generations. Felt moment of her own: the small joy of being trusted by a child (scene 3) and the tenderness of overhearing the Relay's song (scene 4). Power appears once, as protection (eleven minutes as a wall), and does not decide the dispute.

A distinctive, emotionally disciplined encounter with an ancient relay whose refusal is treated as a coherent epistemic position rather than malice. The draft protects Bryn's and the Relay's agency, gives Illuminara an operationally loving role, and lands on a promising positive outcome. Before final, the proof logic, Kaspar's change of course and the day-11/day-13 decision chain need to be made causal and visible.

R14 check: the carrying scenes are Bryn's unplanned question (scene 4) and Kaspar owning the breach (scene 5). Turn is understanding (the Relay's certainty dissolves; Kaspar changes the question from 'is it cruel' to 'is it counting'), not power: the wall only buys one breath. Love in action: Illuminara stands where the defence lands, with the Relay's consent, and designs an arrangement in which nobody has to be believed. Felt moments kept: trust from a child; the tenderness of overhearing the song; warm rock. Speakers: five (Illuminara, Kaspar, Ines, the Relay, Bryn); the Council and the pickets do not speak. Remaining costs: Kaspar resigns, the line must stay manned, the makers cannot be told, the correspondence will take generations. Open to the critic: scene 4 and 5 are denser than scenes 1-3; length is about 3,100 words by label-inclusive count.

All three ranked T02 requests are resolved in the story itself. The Relay no longer treats surprise as proof of an external mind: it treats lost certainty as insufficient licence for an irreversible Reseeding and authors a reversible, observable pause with an explicit right to resume the count. Kaspar now meets the Relay directly, sets a limited fleet condition, tests it against the silent count and the predeclared line response, owns the breach at political cost and preserves her caution. The day-ten breach, day-eleven vote and day-thirteen withdrawal are dramatized, while the physical harm of Reseeding is made concrete. The revision keeps Bryn's question, Ines's linguistic discovery, the Relay's agency, Illuminara's protective rather than deciding role, and a real positive result with unresolved cost. No new priority criticism is warranted before AUTHOR_FINAL.

R14 check at lock: the turn is understanding, not power. The Relay's certainty dissolves under Bryn's unplanned question and it chooses a reversible, checkable pause; Kaspar changes by evidence (a silent count, a defence that behaves as announced, a breach she publicly owns) while keeping her caution and paying with her office; Illuminara protects (stands where the defence lands, with the Relay's consent) and never supplies the question or the decision. Real positive result: the Reseeding is withdrawn by the Relay itself, the forty thousand keep their lives and rolls, the fleet holds then goes home, a correspondence begins. Remaining costs kept: Kaspar's resignation, the manned line, the makers who cannot be told, generations of slow letters. Protected unchanged: the 4,007 polished answers, Ines's responsive mood, Bryn's failed prepared questions, the Relay's right to refuse and to resume the count.

final_critic_line: Illuminara helps the Relay replace irreversible certainty with a reversible, publicly testable choice, protects the breach without seizing anyone's decision, and lets Bryn, Kaspar and the Relay freely build a future in which forty thousand people keep their lives and the long silence becomes correspondence.
